# Real Korea Trip

> Step-by-step guides for T-money, trains, apps, food and the cities beyond Seoul — written for first-time visitors to South Korea. Every guide shows a last-checked date and links to official sources (Korea Tourism Organization, Seoul Metropolitan Government, transport operators).

- Site: https://realkoreatrip.com/
- Editorial policy: facts come from official sources and are dated; recommendations are labeled as our opinion. See https://realkoreatrip.com/about/
- Contact for corrections: realkoreatrip76@gmail.com

## Start Here

- [Bringing Medicine into Korea: Limits, Prescriptions and the Narcotics Permit](https://realkoreatrip.com/bringing-medicine-into-korea/): Bringing medicine into Korea — up to 6 bottles or a 3-month supply, proof you need, and which drugs (like zolpidem or Ritalin) need an MFDS permit first. (last checked 2026-10-30, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Seoul Itinerary for 3, 4 or 5 Days: A First-Timer's Plan](https://realkoreatrip.com/seoul-itinerary-3-4-5-days/): A 3-, 4- or 5-day Seoul itinerary for first-timers — palaces, Bukchon, Namsan, and day trips to the DMZ, Nami Island and Jeonju, planned around closing days. (last checked 2026-10-29, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Korea Public Holidays 2027: Dates, Long Weekends and What Closes](https://realkoreatrip.com/korea-public-holidays-2027/): Korea's 2027 holidays: Seollal Feb 6–9 (including a substitute day), Chuseok Sep 14–16, ten 3+ day breaks for a five-day workweek, plus closure tips. (last checked 2026-10-27, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Best Time to Visit Korea: Month-by-Month Weather](https://realkoreatrip.com/best-time-to-visit-korea/): When to visit Korea, from official 30-year weather averages — Seoul's temperature and rain for every month, plus Busan and Jeju, season by season. (last checked 2026-10-25, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Emergency Help in Korea: 112, 119, 1330 and English-Speaking Hospitals](https://realkoreatrip.com/emergency-help-korea/): Which number to call in Korea and what to say — 112 police, 119 fire and ambulance with interpreters, the 1330 travel hotline, lost and found and hospitals. (last checked 2026-10-25)
- [K-ETA Explained: Do You Need One to Visit Korea?](https://realkoreatrip.com/k-eta-korea/): Nationals of 22 countries and regions are K-ETA-exempt until Dec 31, 2026 (KST), including the US, UK and Japan. Check eligibility, fees and fake sites. (last checked 2026-10-23)
- [Korea First-Timer Checklist: What to Sort Before You Fly](https://realkoreatrip.com/korea-first-time-checklist/): What to sort before your first Korea trip — K-ETA, the e-Arrival Card, Q-CODE, customs, plugs, data, money and emergency numbers, from official sources. (last checked 2026-10-23)

## Getting Around

- [Gimpo Airport to Seoul: AREX, Subway Line 9, Bus or Taxi](https://realkoreatrip.com/gimpo-airport-to-seoul/): How to get from Gimpo Airport into Seoul — AREX to Seoul Station from ₩1,750, Line 9 express to Gangnam, limousine buses and taxi estimates, from official sources. (last checked 2026-10-28, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Seoul to Busan: KTX vs Express Bus vs Flight](https://realkoreatrip.com/seoul-to-busan-ktx-bus-flight/): Seoul to Busan compared — KTX ₩54,400 (about 3 hours per KTO), express bus from ₩29,100 in about 4 hours, or a scheduled 65–75 minute flight. (last checked 2026-10-29, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Taxis in Korea: Fares, Apps and How to Get One](https://realkoreatrip.com/taxis-in-korea/): How taxis work in Korea for visitors — Seoul's official fares and night surcharges, the apps that take foreign cards, International Taxi and paying without tips. (last checked 2026-10-25)
- [How to Book KTX Train Tickets in Korea as a Foreigner](https://realkoreatrip.com/how-to-book-ktx-korea/): Book Korea's KTX trains in English — where to buy, when tickets open, current fares, refunds and the KORAIL PASS, after the 2026 KTX–SRT merger. (last checked 2026-10-23)
- [Seoul Subway Guide for First-Timers: Fares, Tickets and Transfers](https://realkoreatrip.com/seoul-subway-guide/): How the Seoul subway works for visitors — current fares, T-money vs single tickets vs the Climate Card pass, transfer discounts, and the tap-out rule people miss. (last checked 2026-10-23)
- [How to Get a T-money Card in Korea (and Top It Up)](https://realkoreatrip.com/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/): Where to buy Korea's transit card, how much it costs, how to top it up with cash, and the bus mistake that costs first-time visitors their transfer discount. (last checked 2026-10-22)
- [Incheon Airport to Seoul: AREX Train vs Airport Bus vs Taxi](https://realkoreatrip.com/incheon-airport-to-seoul/): The three main ways from Incheon Airport into Seoul, with current fares, journey times and which one fits your arrival time, luggage and budget. (last checked 2026-10-22)

## Destinations

- [Andong Travel Guide: Hahoe Village, Confucian Academies and Jjimdak](https://realkoreatrip.com/andong-travel-guide/): A first-timer's guide to Andong — Hahoe Village (adults ₩5,000), the 14:00 mask dance show, Dosan and Byeongsan Seowon, KTX-Eum from Seoul and what to eat. (last checked 2026-10-30)
- [Gangneung Travel Guide: Ojukheon, Beaches, Coffee and Chodang Tofu](https://realkoreatrip.com/gangneung-travel-guide/): A first-timer's guide to Gangneung — Ojukheon (adults ₩3,000, last entry 17:00), Seongyojang, Gyeongpo Beach, Anmok coffee street and Chodang sundubu tofu. (last checked 2026-10-30)
- [Myeongdong Guide: Shopping, Street Food Stalls and Myeongdong Cathedral](https://realkoreatrip.com/myeongdong-guide/): A first-timer's guide to Myeongdong — shopping streets, licensed street stalls and prices, Myeongdong Cathedral's 09:00 English Mass, and help in English. (last checked 2026-10-31)
- [Tongyeong Travel Guide: Cable Car, Island Ferries and Chungmu Gimbap](https://realkoreatrip.com/tongyeong-travel-guide/): A first-timer's guide to Tongyeong — the cable car up Mireuksan (adults ₩17,000 return), the ferry to Hansan-do, Sebyeonggwan Hall, Dongpirang and Chungmu gimbap. (last checked 2026-10-30, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Lotte World and Seoul Sky: Tickets, Hours and Tips for One Day in Jamsil](https://realkoreatrip.com/lotte-world-seoul-sky-guide/): Lotte World tickets from ₩64,000 for adults (19+), Seoul Sky ₩33,000 (13+), plus Magic Pass, hours, the Sky Bridge and how to do both in a day. (last checked 2026-10-29)
- [DMZ Tour from Seoul: Third Tunnel, Dora Observatory and the JSA](https://realkoreatrip.com/dmz-tour-from-seoul/): Visit the DMZ from Seoul on your own — the Third Tunnel tour from Imjingak (₩12,200), passport rules, Monday closing, getting there and the JSA status. (last checked 2026-10-29, updated 2026-10-31)
- [N Seoul Tower Guide: Tickets, Hours, Cable Car and How to Get There](https://realkoreatrip.com/n-seoul-tower-guide/): N Seoul Tower tickets and hours — observatory ₩29,000 for adults, Namsan cable car ₩15,000 return, plus the free shuttle, buses 01A/01B and walking routes. (last checked 2026-10-29, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Nami Island from Seoul: Tickets, Ferry Times and How to Get There](https://realkoreatrip.com/nami-island-from-seoul/): Visiting Nami Island from Seoul — ₩19,000 tickets with the ferry, ferry times, the ITX train to Gapyeong, the shuttle bus and ₩13,000 early or late tickets. (last checked 2026-10-29, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Bukchon Hanok Village Visiting Hours and Rules: The 10:00–17:00 Red Zone and ₩100,000 Fine](https://realkoreatrip.com/bukchon-hanok-village-visiting-rules/): Bukchon has tourist visiting hours — 10:00–17:00 in the Bukchon-ro 11-gil red zone, a ₩100,000 fine, tour bus limits and how to visit a residential area politely. (last checked 2026-10-27, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon): Tickets, Booking and English Tours](https://realkoreatrip.com/changdeokgung-huwon-guide/): How to visit Changdeokgung and its Secret Garden (Huwon) — when online tickets open, the ₩5,000 garden fee, timed English tours, Monday closing and seasonal hours. (last checked 2026-10-27)
- [Gyeongbokgung Palace Guide: Hours, Tickets, Free Hanbok Entry and the Guard Ceremony](https://realkoreatrip.com/gyeongbokgung-palace-guide/): Seoul's main royal palace from official sources — seasonal hours, the ₩3,000 adult ticket, free entry in hanbok, English tours and the gate guard ceremony. (last checked 2026-10-26)
- [Busan Travel Guide: Beaches, Gamcheon Village and Jagalchi Market](https://realkoreatrip.com/busan-travel-guide/): A first-timer's guide to Busan — Haeundae Beach, Gamcheon Culture Village, Jagalchi Market, the city's signature pork soup and getting there by KTX. (last checked 2026-10-23)
- [Gyeongju Travel Guide: Korea's Ancient Silla Capital in One Day](https://realkoreatrip.com/gyeongju-travel-guide/): A first-timer's guide to Gyeongju — the Silla UNESCO sites, Bulguksa Temple, the royal tombs, Donggung Palace at night, English guiding and a one-day plan. (last checked 2026-10-23)
- [Jeju Island Travel Guide: Volcanoes, Hallasan and Black Pork](https://realkoreatrip.com/jeju-travel-guide/): A first-timer's guide to Jeju — the UNESCO volcanic sites, Seongsan Ilchulbong, booking and timing a Hallasan summit hike, Jeju's buses and black pork. (last checked 2026-10-23)
- [Jeonju Day Trip from Seoul: Hanok Village Guide](https://realkoreatrip.com/jeonju-day-trip-from-seoul/): How to do Jeonju in a day from Seoul — the KTX from Yongsan, getting to the Hanok Village, Gyeonggijeon Shrine and what to eat, checked against official sources. (last checked 2026-10-23)

## Food

- [Gwangjang Market Food Guide: Hours, Dishes and How to Visit](https://realkoreatrip.com/gwangjang-market-food-guide/): Eating at Gwangjang Market in Seoul — food alley hours (09:00–23:00, open year-round), dishes to try, the gates to use and what Seoul announced on fair prices. (last checked 2026-10-31)
- [Noryangjin Fish Market: How to Buy Seafood and Eat It Upstairs](https://realkoreatrip.com/noryangjin-fish-market-guide/): How Noryangjin Fish Market in Seoul works — buy seafood at a stall, eat it at a restaurant upstairs, check auction prices and how the 24-hour recall works. (last checked 2026-10-31)
- [Korean BBQ for First-Timers: How to Grill, Wrap and Order](https://realkoreatrip.com/korean-bbq-guide/): How a Korean BBQ restaurant works — samgyeopsal, pork galbi and bulgogi explained, how to make a lettuce wrap, what to order to finish and how to call staff. (last checked 2026-10-26, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Korean Street Food Guide: Tteokbokki, Gimbap, Fish Cakes and Winter Snacks](https://realkoreatrip.com/korean-street-food/): What to order at a Korean street stall or bunsik shop — tteokbokki, sundae, gimbap, fish cakes, winter hotteok and fish-shaped buns — and where to find them. (last checked 2026-10-26, updated 2026-10-31)
- [What to Eat in Jeonju: Bibimbap, Bean Sprout Soup and Nambu Market](https://realkoreatrip.com/what-to-eat-in-jeonju/): Jeonju's signature dishes explained — Jeonju bibimbap, kongnamul gukbap with moju, pisundae and Nambu Market — based on Jeonju City's own food guides. (last checked 2026-10-23)

## Local Tips

- [Jjimjilbang for First-Timers: Korean Spa Rules, Prices and Etiquette](https://realkoreatrip.com/jjimjilbang-guide-korea/): How a Korean jjimjilbang works — the locker key, separate baths, shared sauna rooms, time limits, example prices from ₩22,000 and the rules to know. (last checked 2026-10-31)
- [Pharmacies in Korea: Buying Medicine as a Visitor](https://realkoreatrip.com/pharmacies-in-korea/): How Korean pharmacies (약국) work for visitors — what you can buy without a prescription, finding a pharmacy open late at night, and getting help in English. (last checked 2026-10-31)
- [Korean Convenience Stores: Medicine, Alcohol Age, Tax Refunds and More](https://realkoreatrip.com/korea-convenience-store-guide/): What Korean convenience stores sell and do — 13 approved medicines, the alcohol age rule, instant tax refunds at CU, T-money, ATMs and parcels. (last checked 2026-10-29, updated 2026-10-31)
- [10 Apps for Traveling in Korea: What Each One Does](https://realkoreatrip.com/korea-travel-apps/): The apps that make a Korea trip easier — Naver Map, Papago, KORAIL+, K-ETA, taxi apps that take foreign cards, a prepaid travel card and two official safety apps. (last checked 2026-10-25)
- [Korean Etiquette for Travelers: Restaurants, Table Manners and the Subway](https://realkoreatrip.com/korean-etiquette/): The etiquette that matters on a Korea trip, from official sources — no tipping, free side-dish refills, table manners with elders, and Seoul Metro's subway rules. (last checked 2026-10-25, updated 2026-10-31)
- [Tax Refund in Korea: How Visitors Get Money Back on Shopping](https://realkoreatrip.com/korea-tax-refund-guide/): Who can claim a tax refund in Korea, the ₩15,000 minimum, instant refunds in stores, and what to do at the airport so you don't lose your refund. (last checked 2026-10-23)
- [Paying in Korea: Foreign Cards, Cash and What Still Needs Won](https://realkoreatrip.com/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/): Where a foreign card works in Korea, where you still need won cash, and how to get won at Incheon Airport — checked against official sources. (last checked 2026-10-23)
- [eSIM vs SIM Card vs Pocket Wi-Fi in Korea: Which One Should You Get?](https://realkoreatrip.com/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/): eSIM, SIM card, pocket Wi-Fi or free Wi-Fi in Korea — prices from the carriers' own sites, when you need a Korean number, and how to choose. (last checked 2026-10-22)
- [How to Use Naver Map in Korea (and Why Google Maps Isn't Enough)](https://realkoreatrip.com/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/): Google Maps gave us transit routes in Seoul but no walking or driving directions. Here's how to set up and use Naver Map in English, step by step. (last checked 2026-10-22)
